f.title: Treat as serious any AE meeting the seriousness criteria, including medically important events
f.statement: A serious adverse event is any adverse event that results in death, is life-threatening, requires hospitalisation or prolongs it, results in permanent or significant disability or incapacity, or causes a congenital anomaly or malformation. For notification purposes, events that from a medical point of view may endanger the subject or require intervention to prevent one of those outcomes are also treated as serious. The same criteria define a serious adverse reaction (definition 41).

f.title: Classify as SUSAR any SAE with a reasonable possibility of causality not described in the IB or SmPC
f.statement: An unexpected adverse reaction is one whose nature or severity is not consistent with the investigational product information, i.e. not described in the investigator's brochure and/or summary of product characteristics. A suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction (SUSAR) is any serious adverse event with at least a reasonable possibility of a causal relationship with the investigational product whose nature or severity is not described in the investigator's brochure and/or the SmPC.

f.title: Failure to report adverse events, or late reporting, is an infringement subject to sanctions
f.statement: Failure to comply with the obligation to communicate adverse events of the investigational product to OGITT of the INS, and communicating adverse effects after the deadline set in the Regulation, are infringements. Infringements are sanctioned by OGITT with a warning, a fine of 0.5 to 100 tax units (UIT), closure of a site for a trial, cancellation of the site registration or of the trial, or restriction of the investigator; fines are payable within 15 business days of notification of the sanction.
